title: Urological Supply Program — Program Criteria and Documentation by Catheter Program
content:
The Urological Supply Program enrolls a patient in one of six catheter programs. Each program has its own entry condition, its own catheter code and its own documentation requirement beyond the supply order. This sheet sets those out for every program side by side.

## Entry conditions

| Program | Condition | Further requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Straight Intermittent Catheter Program (A4351) | permanent urinary retention or neurogenic bladder | method: sterile intermittent self-catheterization |
| Coudé Tip Intermittent Catheter Program (A4352) | as straight program | documentation: straight tip cannot be inserted (for example prostatic enlargement or urethral stricture) |
| Closed-System Catheter Program (A4353) | as straight program | documentation: closed-system criteria — nursing facility resident, immunosuppression, vesico-ureteral reflux on antibiotics, spinal cord injured pregnant patient, or the program's required number of infections in 12 months on sterile intermittent |
| Indwelling Foley Catheter Program (A4338) | permanent retention or incontinence not manageable otherwise | method: indwelling catheter changed by a nurse or caregiver |
| All-Silicone Indwelling Catheter Program (A4344) | as indwelling Foley program | documentation: latex allergy or recurrent encrustation |
| Male External Catheter Program (A4349) | permanent urinary incontinence | sex: male; skin: intact penile skin |

## Program figures

- **Catheter code** — the code of the program's catheter.
- **Criteria documentation** — the documentation the program needs beyond the order.
- **Infections required** — infections in 12 months on sterile intermittent catheters that qualify the closed system on that ground (count); 0 when not applicable.
- **Permanence period** — the expected minimum duration of the condition for it to count as permanent (months).
- **Prior-authorization program** — whether the program falls under the coverage's urological prior-authorization requirement.

| Program | Catheter code | Criteria documentation | Infections required | Permanence period (months) | Prior-authorization program |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Straight Intermittent Catheter Program (A4351) | A4351 | none | 0 | 3 | yes |
| Coudé Tip Intermittent Catheter Program (A4352) | A4352 | straight failure documented | 0 | 3 | yes |
| Closed-System Catheter Program (A4353) | A4353 | closed-system criteria | 2 | 3 | yes |
| Indwelling Foley Catheter Program (A4338) | A4338 | none beyond order | 0 | 3 | yes |
| All-Silicone Indwelling Catheter Program (A4344) | A4344 | latex allergy or encrustation | 0 | 3 | yes |
| Male External Catheter Program (A4349) | A4349 | none | 0 | 3 | yes |

## Reading the sheet

- "As straight program" means the Coudé Tip and Closed-System programs carry the same condition as the Straight Intermittent program — permanent urinary retention or neurogenic bladder — and add their own documentation.
- "As indwelling Foley program" means the All-Silicone program carries the Indwelling Foley condition — permanent retention or incontinence not manageable otherwise — and adds documentation of latex allergy or recurrent encrustation.
- The infection count of 2 is the Closed-System figure; every other program shows 0 because the infection ground does not apply to it.
- Every one of the six programs shows a permanence period of 3 months and falls under the urological prior-authorization requirement.
